name: Snapchat
summary: Snap can train its generative AI on your public Snaps (Spotlight, public Stories, Snap Map) and uses My AI chats to improve its products. Public-content use is on by default and can be switched off.

training.details: Snap may use images, video, audio and text you post publicly on Snapchat, such as Spotlight, public Stories and Snap Map, to develop, train and improve its generative AI models. An in-app Generative AI setting (“Allow use of public content”) is on by default and stops this going forward. Separately, content you share with My AI is kept until you delete it and is used to improve Snap’s products, including the models behind My AI, and to personalise ads; there is no setting to stop that, but you can clear your My AI data (deletion can take up to 30 days). Private Snaps and chats with friends are not part of the public-content training, but you may still appear in other people’s public posts.

regionNotes.EU: You can also use your GDPR right to object by contacting Snap’s Data Protection Officer.
regionNotes.UK: You can also use your UK GDPR right to object by contacting Snap’s Data Protection Officer.

optOuts.title: Turn off “Allow use of public content” for generative AI
optOuts.description: An in-app setting with no web version, so NoTrain can only guide you. The link opens Snap’s help page. It does not cover My AI chats.
steps: Open Snapchat, tap your profile icon, then the gear icon to open Settings.
Scroll to Privacy Controls and open the Generative AI settings.
Turn off “Allow use of public content”.
Optional: to delete past My AI chats, use “Clear My AI Data” in Settings.
optOuts.effect: Snap stops using your public content to train its generative AI from now on. Past training isn’t undone, My AI chats are still used, and you may still appear in others’ public posts.
